channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: China and Central Asia Expand Air Connectivity to Boost Trade and Tourism
item.description: China and Central Asian aviation officials met in Tashkent to enhance existing agreements and plan expansions. Kazakhstan will increase weekly flights to 180 and add new routes, while Uzbekistan will raise its flights to China to 114. Air Astana and China Southern Airlines formed a strategic partnership.

item.title: Turkish TRT Channel to Showcase Khorezm's Cultural Richness to International Audience
item.description: A TRT film crew visited Uzbekistan's Khorezm region to produce a special program on its historical and cultural heritage, traditions, and tourism potential. Filming in the ancient city of Khiva, the crew captured the 'Lazgi' dance and traditional music. The program aims to enhance Khorezm's international tourism appeal.

item.title: Uzbekistan President to Attend COP31 Climate Summit in Turkey
item.description: President Shavkat Mirziyoyev of Uzbekistan will attend the 31st session of the Conference of the Parties to the UN Framework Convention on Climate Change (COP31) in Turkey, upon the invitation of President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan. The conference, running from November 9-20, focuses on combating environmental threats and transitioning to a green economy.

item.title: Sadyr Japarov Applies to Run for Kyrgyzstan Presidency Again in 2027 Election
item.description: Sadyr Japarov has submitted an application to run for president of Kyrgyzstan in the upcoming election scheduled for January 27, 2027. He aims to secure a second term in office. Currently, six individuals have declared their candidacy for the presidency.

item.title: Iran Denies US Claims of Talks, States Hormuz Strait Closure Condition
item.description: Mohsen Rezaei, secretary of Iran’s Supreme National Security Council, has called US claims of ongoing negotiations with Tehran a "complete lie." He stated that the Strait of Hormuz will remain closed until Iran's seven announced conditions are met. Rezaei asserted that US claims aim to ease economic pressure and lower oil prices, and that Iran awaits a clear response to its conditions.

item.title: Afghan UN Envoy: Denying Girls Education is Betrayal and Blow to Future
item.description: Afghanistan's UN Representative Nasir Ahmad Faiq stated that denying girls education and restricting boys' access to modern sciences is a betrayal of a generation and harmful to Afghanistan's future. He emphasized education as a human right crucial for progress and fighting poverty.

item.title: Outdated Standards Hinder Uzbekistan's WTO Accession, Deputies Raise Concerns
item.description: Uzbekistan's path to joining the World Trade Organization is being obstructed by outdated national standards, according to lawmakers. A parliamentary inquiry has been sent to the head of the "Uzstandard" Agency, highlighting issues with technical regulation, digitalization, and corruption risks. Approximately half of Uzbekistan's 33,000 active standards are reportedly obsolete or do not meet international requirements.

item.title: Almaty Region Reports 31% Decrease in Fatalities Amidst Widespread Camera Surveillance
item.description: The Almaty region has reported a 31% decrease in fatalities, attributed in part to the deployment of nearly 9,500 surveillance cameras. Since the beginning of the year, these cameras have recorded traffic violations resulting in fines totaling 11.5 billion tenge. Regional officials highlighted the role of digital infrastructure in enhancing public safety and reducing accidents.

item.title: Kazakhstan to reform legislation on public council activities
item.description: Kazakhstan's Ministry of Culture and Information held the first meeting of a working group to improve legislation regulating public councils. The initiative aligns with President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev's directive to enhance public participation in governance. Discussions focused on identifying key issues and developing proposals to increase the effectiveness of these councils.

item.title: Uzbekistan enhances judicial protection guarantees for citizens and businesses
item.description: Uzbekistan's lower house of parliament discussed amendments to legislation aimed at strengthening judicial protection for citizens and entrepreneurs. The proposed changes, which will affect the Civil Procedure Code and laws on state duty and insolvency, seek to eliminate legal gaps and streamline court proceedings. Specific measures address civil status record corrections and insolvency procedures.

item.title: Uzbekistan's President discusses climate adaptation cooperation with Green Climate Fund
item.description: Uzbekistan's President Shavkat Mirziyoyev met with the Executive Director of the Green Climate Fund. The discussion focused on expanding cooperation in climate change adaptation and attracting climate finance. The meeting highlighted Uzbekistan's commitment to addressing climate challenges and securing international funding for related initiatives.

item.title: Ukraine, Russia, and US Resume Peace Talks in Abu Dhabi After Nine-Month Hiatus
item.description: Ukraine, Russia, and the US have resumed three-way peace negotiations in Abu Dhabi following a nine-month pause. Discussions, which lasted over four hours on the first day, are set to continue. Delegations include high-level representatives from each country, with European nations participating in separate consultations.

item.title: IMF Team Assesses Tajikistan's Fiscal Transparency During Visit
item.description: An International Monetary Fund delegation is in Tajikistan to evaluate public finances. The IMF team met with the parliament's economy and finance committee to discuss financial transparency, data accessibility, accountability, and budget planning. Both sides expressed readiness to strengthen cooperation to enhance transparency. The visit concludes on November 11.

item.title: Afghan University Graduates Face Widespread Unemployment
item.description: Many educated Afghans find their degrees no longer guarantee employment. A 29-year-old journalism graduate shared his struggles, noting that even when applying for advertised positions, many are not shortlisted. He described unemployment as a heavy burden. World Bank data indicates youth unemployment among men aged 15-29 reached 22% in 2023, nearly triple the 2020 rate.

item.title: ETIM Poses Transit, Recruitment, and Propaganda Threats to Kazakhstan
item.description: Experts assess the risks of transnational terrorism, noting the East Turkestan Islamic Movement (ETIM) has evolved from a regional political demand group to an internationally linked terrorist network. Its potential threats to Kazakhstan include transit routes, recruitment activities, and online propaganda, especially given Kazakhstan's border with China and Central Asia's mention in UN documents as an area of ETIM activity.

item.title: Almaty Region Sees 31% Drop in Mortality Rate Due to Public Safety Cameras
item.description: The Almaty region has reported a 31% decrease in its mortality rate, attributed to the installation of approximately 9,500 public safety cameras. These cameras have also generated 11.5 billion tenge in fines for traffic violations since the beginning of the year. The digital initiatives aim to enhance public safety and reduce road accidents.

item.title: Uzbekistan Imposes New Environmental Rules on Greenhouses Near Tashkent
item.description: Uzbekistan has introduced new environmental regulations for greenhouses in Tashkent and five surrounding districts. Coal-fired facilities must switch to cleaner energy sources like natural gas, electricity, or solar power by December 1, or meet strict pollution controls. These measures aim for more environmentally friendly operations in the designated ecological zone.

item.title: Osh and Gomel Establish Sister City Partnership
item.description: Osh, Kyrgyzstan, and Gomel, Belarus, have officially become sister cities following the signing of a memorandum at the first Kyrgyzstan-Belarus regional forum. The agreement aims to foster mutually beneficial partnerships in trade, economy, investment, culture, humanitarian ties, education, and tourism.

item.title: Kazakhstan Introduces Online IIN Application for Foreigners in One Day
item.description: Foreigners and stateless persons temporarily staying in Kazakhstan can now apply for and amend their Individual Identification Number (IIN) online via the QazETA app. This pilot project, launched under a Ministry of Internal Affairs order, aims to process applications within one working day.

item.title: Afghan and Iranian Officials Discuss Expanding Bilateral Economic Cooperation
item.description: Afghan and Iranian officials met to discuss expanding bilateral economic cooperation, focusing on implementing agreements from a recent visit to Iran. Iran expressed readiness to cooperate in oil and gas, energy, agriculture, and industrial development. Afghanistan's General Directorate of State-Owned Companies aims to translate proposed cooperation areas into practical initiatives.

item.title: Germany Offers Jobs to Uzbek Builders with Salaries Over 3,400 Euros
item.description: German Railways is offering construction specialist positions to Uzbek citizens, with salaries exceeding 3,400 Euros. Successful candidates will receive eight months of free German language training. This initiative aims to fill vacant positions within the company and provide employment opportunities for skilled workers from Uzbekistan.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan and Belarus Aim to Reach $500 Million in Trade Volume
item.description: Kyrgyzstan and Belarus held the 13th meeting of their joint intergovernmental commission on trade and economic cooperation. Both sides expressed confidence that these events will contribute to expanding future cooperation. Bilateral trade has grown nearly fourfold since 2021. The roadmap aims to increase mutual trade turnover to $500 million by 2030.

item.title: Russia to Launch Comprehensive Digital Profile for Foreigners on December 1
item.description: Russia's Ministry of Internal Affairs plans to fully launch a comprehensive digital profile for foreigners on December 1. This resource, already operating in a test mode since July, will accumulate information, including biometric data, from border checkpoints. The initiative aims to improve the management of foreign citizens within the country.

item.title: Uzbekistan's Central Bank Sees No Major Inflation Risk from Sugar Import Quotas
item.description: Uzbekistan's Central Bank Deputy Chairman Nodirbek Achilov stated that the introduction of a 300,000-ton annual sugar import quota is unlikely to cause significant food inflation. The bank forecasts a further decrease in food inflation in the coming year, with sugar prices remaining relatively stable. Sugar is one of 517 goods and services in the consumer basket.

item.title: Russia, US, and Ukraine Conclude First Day of Trilateral Security Talks in Abu Dhabi
item.description: Delegations from Russia, the United States, and Ukraine finished their first day of trilateral talks in Abu Dhabi after four and a half hours of discussions. The talks are scheduled to resume on Wednesday. Key aspects of establishing a new continental security system in the post-conflict era are expected to be discussed.

item.title: President Sadyr Japarov Travels to Moscow for CSTO Security Council Meeting
item.description: Bishkek, November 10 - President Sadyr Japarov traveled to Moscow today, November 10, to participate in the regular meeting of the Collective Security Council of the Collective Security Treaty Organization (CSTO). The leaders will discuss topical issues of international and regional security, and further measures to strengthen collective security.

item.title: Almaty Authorities Investigate 202 Million Tenge Road Project Lacking State Expertise
item.description: Almaty's Road Infrastructure Development Department paid 202 million tenge for a road reconstruction project that bypassed state expertise. A pre-trial investigation into abuse of power has been launched by the city prosecutor's office. The project documentation is deemed unimplementable, and budget funds were allegedly misused.

item.title: Kazakh President Tokayev Arrives in Moscow for CSTO Collective Security Council Summit
item.description: President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev has arrived in Moscow to participate in the CSTO Collective Security Council session. The summit will address security and international issues for member states. Several documents, including a strategy against terrorism until 2030, are expected to be signed.

item.title: Tokayev Focuses on Construction, Inflation Risks, Japarov's Term
item.description: Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev views construction as the sole solution to improve the country's situation. Meanwhile, Sadyr Japarov, 57, has submitted documents to run for president again, raising questions about how many more years he will lead Kyrgyzstan.

item.title: US Defense Secretary Calls Impeachment Effort a 'Ridiculous Show'
item.description: US Defense Secretary Pat Shanahan described the impeachment effort against him by the House of Representatives as a 'ridiculous show' and a 'political game.' He stated that the move sends a message to US troops that their service is a 'crime' and to adversaries that the US punishes military leaders for successful operations.

item.title: Drug Courier Detained in Almaty with Large Quantity of Narcotics
item.description: Almaty police have detained a courier found with a significant amount of powdered drugs packaged in zip-lock bags. The man reportedly sought earnings through Telegram, agreeing to deliver prohibited substances and create 'dead drops.' He was apprehended while attempting to dispose of the evidence upon seeing police.

item.title: Kazakh President Tokayev arrives in Moscow for CSTO security council meeting
item.description: President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev of Kazakhstan has arrived in Moscow to attend the Collective Security Council meeting of the Collective Security Treaty Organization (CSTO). He was met by Russian government officials at the airport. Russia will chair the CSTO in 2026. Earlier, Tokayev met with the CSTO Secretary General.

item.title: Kazakh Language Integrated into WIPO's AI Subtitling System for First Time
item.description: The Kazakh language has been included in the World Intellectual Property Organization's (WIPO) experimental AI-based subtitling system. It is now among 20 available languages, enabling real-time translation of discussions for Kazakh speakers at international forums. This marks a significant step in expanding the language's digital presence.

item.title: Uzbekistan President Signals Further Migration Policy Reforms by 2027
item.description: Uzbekistan's President Shavkat Mirziyoyev announced further changes to the migration system by 2027, following two previous reforms. This comes amid reported corruption issues within the migration agency. The president emphasized creating conditions that value human dignity and ensuring migrants' rights abroad.

item.title: Russia Claims Air Defenses Destroyed 155 Ukrainian Drones Overnight
item.description: Russia's Ministry of Defence reported that its air defense systems intercepted and destroyed 155 Ukrainian drones across various regions overnight. The attacks reportedly caused minor damage and one injury in the Smolensk and Novgorod regions. This incident is part of ongoing tensions and failed peace efforts between Russia and Ukraine.

item.title: Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev Arrives in Moscow for Security Council Meeting
item.description: President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev has arrived in Moscow to participate in a session of the Collective Security Council of the Collective Security Treaty Organization (CSTO). He was met by Russian government officials at the airport. The purpose of his visit is to attend the CSTO meeting.

item.title: Kazakhstan to Investigate Yandex's Data Security Practices
item.description: Kazakhstan's Ministry of Digital Development will conduct an unscheduled inspection of Yandex's legal entities, including Yandex Kazakhstan, Yandex Go, and Yandex Food Kazakhstan, by the end of November. The probe aims to determine where Kazakhstani citizens' personal data is stored and how it is protected. Violations could lead to administrative liability.

item.title: UN Women: Over One-Third of Global Women Live in Climate-Vulnerable Areas
item.description: UN Women reports that over 1.5 billion women and girls worldwide reside in areas susceptible to climate change risks. The climate crisis, coupled with insecure employment and gender inequality, poses serious threats. While most countries acknowledge these risks, few have implemented comprehensive measures to address them.

item.title: Kazakhstan Launches Pilot Project for Online IIN Registration for Foreigners
item.description: Kazakhstan is piloting a project allowing foreigners and stateless persons to obtain and modify their Individual Identification Numbers (IIN) online via the QazETA mobile app. The service, available through the MAQ digital platform, requires biometric identification and checks entry data. The processing time is one working day.

item.title: Putin Urges CSTO to Enhance Military Cooperation Amid International Tensions
item.description: Russian President Vladimir Putin called for the Collective Security Treaty Organization (CSTO) to increase its potential and strengthen military interaction due to ongoing international tensions. He emphasized the need for active cooperation in defense, counter-terrorism, cybercrime, drug trafficking, and illegal migration. A CSTO summit is scheduled for November 11 in Moscow.
